## 2026-10-11 — A duplicate mapping is refused, never an index error (the Bazel program)

**Landed 2026-10-11 as 0b29453e1** (branch `build/dup-mapping`; run 38145210104, full gate.yml on all platforms: green on every job after one re-run of windows / warehouse (a runner filesystem error in the Node module tree during analysis of `//datacube:jupyterlab_test`, which the change does not touch; the same error L7 step 3's run met once); the first run on the tree before the rebase onto datacube-m3, 38122177071, green on every job).
Announced in `docs/IN_FLIGHT.md` the same day (37a3edb2c). The DataCube line reported it while writing tests: a model
holding two mappings of one name, one including another, crashed `compileModel` with an `IndexOutOfBoundsException`
from the normalizer's include ordering instead of a refusal.

1. **The cause, two halves.** `StoreSubstitutionRewrite.resolveAllStores` counted the parsed mappings (a duplicate
   twice) against the names it had ordered (once), read the difference as an include cycle, and indexed the cycle's
   members — none, since every name was ordered. And a parsed mapping never took its slot in the shared element
   namespace: the D6b batch (`docs/STAMP_DISCIPLINE_PROGRAM.md`) covered classes, enums, associations, profiles,
   measures and databases, and mappings slotted last-wins by plain `intern`, so only the cycle check noticed.
2. **The fix.** The cycle check counts the graph's names (`byFqn`): the ordered names are always among them, so a
   difference names a member. `ModelBuilder.ingestLegacyMapping` registers the DSL mapping through `internElement`,
   and the duplicate is refused as a class's is — and BEFORE Phase E reads the index (`ModelIntegrity.refuseDuplicates`,
   called by `Compiler.normalizeLayer`; the engine's order, D6b's "element-identity first"), so a second copy's own
   shape (a self-include, a repeated include) never speaks first: `compileModel` throws "Duplicated element 'w::M'";
   the module path (`parseSources`) drops a same-kind duplicate at parse and reports it, as before, and walls a
   cross-kind collision (a class and a mapping of one name) under the name. The gate's check keeps the arm for a
   graph element shadowing a boot FQN. The normalized product still registers by plain `intern` under the same name.
3. **Not fixed, recorded:** services, `###Data`, connections (a runtime's inline ones too), runtimes and clean-sheet
   mappings still slot last-wins (`docs/PARKED_WORK_LEDGER.md` PARK-25, anchored on the services slot); two include
   spellings of one mapping are refused as a cycle (PARK-26, anchored on the resolved names' count; the audit's find);
   PARK-25 also records a path that is also a package, which the engine refuses ("An element named 'domain' already
   exists in the package 'trades'"; the DataCube line's audit the same day) and lite, registering no package, does not.
4. **Judges.** the six corpus passes against the baseline built from main 741f24f9a the same day: 22 result files identical, 0 differing (`evidence/dup-mapping/corpus_passes_compare.txt`); the render census, main's tree against the change, every JVM lane with the probe: 52543 (lane, dialect, kind, text) entries; 0 differ (`evidence/dup-mapping/render_census_compare.txt`); the local gate 328 targets green on the final tree (`bazel test --lockfile_mode=error //gates:local`); `//parser-equivalence/...` 6 targets green; the lane-membership query empty. The judges' one find: `RelationalMappingIntegrationTest.testDataMutations` named its class
   `model::M`, as its mapping; the engine refuses the pair (one namespace), and so does lite now; the class is `model::Mut`
   and the `//gates:core` lane's census was run again on the fixed tree (the only lane holding the test). The
   parser-equivalence ratchet `own_corpus.matched` moves 2823 → 2832 (the nine elements of the new test models in
   `IncludeRulesTest` joined the own corpus and matched; measured on the tree rebased onto 6e57d350c, whose own models had
   moved it 2814 → 2823).
5. **The parsed model's side maps key by path alone** (`ParsedModel.keyOf`), so a class and a mapping of one name
   share one offset, imports and span entry; parser-equivalence's conformance ratchet caught it on the refusal's own
   test (the planner placed the mapping at the class's offset and asked for a `###Mapping` header). `Sectionize.plan`
   declines such a snippet as not sectionizable, as it declines one that does not parse; the keying, and the
   refusal's position (the recorded element's, where the engine points at the second), are in PARK-25.
6. **The audit** (`evidence/dup-mapping/AUDIT.md`: ready after fixes, 0 blockers, 5 should-fix, 3 nits, every one
   answered): the refusal moved before Phase E (it had reported a self-include as a cycle); the cross-kind and
   self-include cases tested; the wording narrowed to the DSL's mappings and clean-sheet mappings parked; a dangling
   citation and a "below" fixed.

## 2026-10-11 — A `~func` descriptor spelling a type by its package path is refused, as the engine refuses it (the Bazel program)

**Landed 2026-10-11 as eabda91b8** (branch `build/func-descriptor`; run 38152032814, full gate.yml on all platforms: green on every job, 50 of 50, no re-run; main's own run of the previous landing (38147522593, on 0b29453e1) had timed out once in `//warehouse:tests_native` on linux / warehouse (300 s), a job the same commit passed in 38145210104 and again in this run, so its failed job was re-run rather than rolled back).
Announced in `docs/IN_FLIGHT.md` the same day (9a6873d07). The DataCube line's find against legend-engine 4.145.0,
writing the model writer's tests: a relation class mapping's `~func f():meta::pure::metamodel::relation::Relation<Any>[1]`
compiled in lite and failed in the engine.

1. **The engine's rule.** legend-pure's `FunctionDescriptor.validateType` (m3-core, `navigation/function/FunctionDescriptor.java`),
   run by `functionDescriptorToId` on every descriptor the compiler resolves (`compiler/toPureGraph/PureModel.java`,
   the prerequisite pass), allows no package path in a parameter or return type ("Package path not allowed in types:
   <type>") and no function type ("Unsupported type"); a type's arguments are not read (the id keeps the head name).
   The id conversion failing, the compiler looks the raw text up as an element and reports "Can't find the packageable
   element".
2. **Lite.** `MappingFromProtocol.relationFunction` cut the descriptor at its signature and resolved the name alone, so
   the signature's spelling was never read. Now `refuseDescriptorTypes` reads each parameter type's and the return
   type's head name (the multiplicity stripped, the arguments skipped, as the engine does) and refuses a package path
   or a function type through the model door's own channel (`UnsupportedMappingShape`): the text door reports it at
   the element with the descriptor's position, the JSON door as the element's `Unrepresentable`, the module path walls
   the mapping. At every dialect: the signature means nothing in lite beyond the engine's id format, and a model written
   so compiles nowhere. Not touched: the parser's descriptor scan, the activator's `function:` descriptor (parse-only in
   lite), the wire.
3. **Tests.** `RelationFunctionDescriptorTest` (the return type, a parameter type, a function type refused; the
   simple-name form with and without the signature, and a package path inside a type argument, compile); the two
   fixtures that spelled the long form (`RelationMappingWindowSeamTest`, `StackDesignWitnessTest`) rewritten to the
   simple name, the only such texts in the repository (no corpus text uses the form). The parser-equivalence ratchet is unchanged (`own_corpus.matched` 2832) and the
   lane green.
4. **Judges.** the six corpus passes against the baseline built from main 9a6873d07 the same day: 22 result files identical, 0 differing (`evidence/func-descriptor/corpus_passes_compare.txt`); the render census, main's tree against the change, every JVM lane with the probe: 52550 (lane, dialect, kind, text) entries; 0 differ (`evidence/func-descriptor/render_census_compare.txt`); the local gate 329 targets green on the final tree (`bazel test --lockfile_mode=error //gates:local`); `//parser-equivalence/...` 6 targets green; the lane-membership query empty. The main-side census was run twice: the first run's swap to main's
   source left the branch's new test file in place, so main's test library did not build and the core lane's records were
   missing on that side (3384 entries "differ", all absent on main); the chain scripts now remove branch-only files
   during the swap, and the second run is the one compared.
5. **The audit** (`evidence/func-descriptor/AUDIT.md`: ready after fixes, 0 blockers, 5 should-fix, 6 notes, every one
   answered): the JSON door tested (the text's protocol JSON read back and compiled, refused with the engine's phrase);
   a JSON-carried descriptor's spaces removed outside quotes before the scan, as the engine's lexer drops them; PARK-28
   records that the signature itself is never matched against the function's (the engine resolves by the full id
   `f__Relation_1_`, lite by the name alone; the `~src f():R[1]` form drops its tail at parse; the activator's
   `function:` descriptor is parse-only), anchored on the signature cut and pinned in `ParkedWorkLedgerTest`; the
   identity guard's NAME_AFFIX_TEST re-pinned 51 → 52 with the reason (a descriptor TYPE's spelling tested for a package
   path: the engine's rule on text never resolved into a declaration, not a name's affix); a unit type and a type
   variable tested as accepted; the handoff note of 2026-09-02 corrected.
6. **Two differences from the announcement, and one from the engine.** The refusal rides the model door's own channel
   (`UnsupportedMappingShape`): a positioned `ParseException` from text, `Unrepresentable` from JSON, which
   `Compiler.compileModel` reports as `NotImplementedException` (the channel's wording, not this rule's), not the
   `ModelException` the announcement named; and a function type in a parameter or return position is refused too
   ("Unsupported type"), the same `validateType`. Lite's message names the rule and the type where the engine reports
   "Can't find the packageable element '<descriptor>'" at the class mapping (its id conversion fails and the raw text is
   looked up): a deliberate difference, so an engine-fixture comparison of this case sees two messages.

## 2026-10-12 — DataCube one app, steps 1 and 2 and PlanAndRun: the tab, then Python's pages, one app and one path on both hosts (the DataCube + Python line)

The design is `docs/DATACUBE_ONE_APP_DESIGN_2026_10_11.md` (agreed 2026-10-11; §15 PlanAndRun agreed 2026-10-12). PR
#31, merged as 36b72ee13. CI: run 38323008283 on f735d1857, every job green on every platform (52 checks), the branch up
to date with main acd7a1df6; main's own run 38327366349 (dispatched: the push run was skipped by the merged commits'
`[skip ci]`) green. `//gates:local //datacube/... //python/... //parser-equivalence/...` green on the rebased head before
the push (361 pass, 2 of main's guards skipped on macOS).

     a set of them. `demo/boot.ts` is the tab's host; `demo/page.ts`, `engine-page.ts` and `engine-cube.ts` are gone.

     against the model Python holds, runs only that SQL on its DuckDB, and the page reads the rows with the tab's reader.
     Python's own results (`table.execute`, `grid.to_pandas()`) are typed by the plan.

   - `//python:engine_test`, `:frames_test`, `:headless_test`, `:wheel_test`; `//datacube:upload_test`, `:duckdb_test`.
3. **Known, and where it goes** (§15.7): two DuckDB patch versions (1.5.4 in the tab, 1.5.5 in Python); Python's
   results come back whole (streaming a follow-up); a query's own `sourceUrl('file:...')` accepted on Python (the user,
   §15.4); a Variant stored as a STRUCT under `SELECT *` comes back raw until the Compiler Rewrite line's egress fix

## 2026-10-11 — DataCube headless in Python: DataCube's own code in V8, planned by the native library, run on Python's DuckDB, no WebAssembly (the DataCube + Python line)

The design is `docs/DATACUBE_HEADLESS_PYTHON_DESIGN_2026_10_11.md`. The user agreed it and ruled §10: one package, V8,
before the model plan's Python calls, the rename. It was reviewed by the Plan Gen / Exec Split and Compiler Rewrite
lines. The evidence is in `docs/datacube-headless-evidence-2026-10-11/`. Branch `datacube-headless`, 25 commits and this one.
CI: run 38177320130 (warehouse, checks, datacube, ui and parser_equivalence on all platforms) green but for Windows'
datacube lane, a Windows-only path in the new runner test, fixed and run again in 38178422811 (datacube on all
platforms), green; the only change after them is main's IN_FLIGHT line, rebased onto. `//gates:local` green before.

1. **What it is.**
   - Python runs DataCube's non-screen TypeScript in V8 (mini-racer 0.14.1).
   - DataCube's own planner plans over its worker protocol (`datacube/src/planner-protocol.ts`). The host answers each
     request kind with the native library's function that delegates to the same `Boundary` function as the tab's
     export. Three were added for this: `lite_plan_text_held`, `lite_relation_type_text_held`, `lite_test_data_sql`.
   - Its queries run on Python's DuckDB, through `DuckDbEngine` and Arrow IPC.
   - WebAssembly is deleted from the V8 context before anything loads.
   - DataCube's side is `datacube/src/headless/`: the web layer to its standards, the host's worker and connection, and
     the grid. Python's side is `legend_lite/_headless.py`: V8 on a loop of legend-lite's own, and the one table of
     request kinds, which is also the start-up check against the library's exports.
2. **What a person gets.**
   - `grid.view()`: what a page's grid shows, as DataCube computes it, with its configuration folded in and its columns
     laid out as the screen lays them out.
   - `grid.relation`: its rows at their finest level, as Create a Class makes them.
   - `grid.to_pandas()`: every one of those rows, from the frames' own database.
   - These are safe inside a notebook's running loop.
   - `pip install legend-lite[datacube]` gives this; the wheel carries the bundle.
   - `WasmPlanner` is renamed `LitePlanner`, with Plan Gen.
3. **The lane, `//datacube:headless_test`, in `//gates:warehouse`.**
   - **67 of DataCube's test files, 1,122 tests, all passing**, the same count Node runs for them. Each runs through the
     production paths, built with a `headless` condition (`#test-host`) that swaps only where a test's planner and
     database come from.
   - The 14 files that mixed screen, HTTP or Node-reference tests were each split in two (`-dom`, `-http`, `-node`):
     324 tests, as before.
   - `headless_roster_test` keeps every test file in the lane, left out by name with a reason, or Node-only by what it
     imports.
   - **The judges are held to Node's own:**
     - `node-assert.ts` against `node:assert/strict`, over 66+ value pairs and every expectation kind;
     - `node-test.ts` against Node's own node:test, which runs the same suite in a child Node, and its mock timers too;
     - the web layer against Node's built-ins, and against the DOM standard alone where Node 22 departs from it.
   - The lane asserts no test was skipped.
   - The host's own checks: the request kinds both ways, no WebAssembly, a plan through the worker run on DuckDB, the
     memory cap, a timeout, every `setTimeout` form, and a registered file's folder.
4. **Reviews and audit.**
   - Plan Gen: found two worker kinds answered by other functions than the tab's (`plan`, `relationType`); now closed.
   - Compiler Rewrite: the lane in warehouse, the roster guard, parser_equivalence in CI.
   - The branch's audit: 2 blockers (the grid's configuration not folded in; two locks in opposite orders) and 9
     should-fix, every one answered (design §14).
   - Windows CI found the test-imports generator's command line past 8191 characters with the split's files. It now
     takes a `params_file`. And the live node:test comparison handed Node its reporter as a drive path, which a module
     specifier cannot be; it is now a `file:` URL.
5. **Upstream.** mini-racer's `setTimeout` throws for a delay of 0 or less and never fires with none
   (https://github.com/bpcreech/PyMiniRacer/issues/97: not by design, not reported before, not fixed in 0.14.1). The
   host holds each delay to a millisecond until the pin moves past the fix.
6. **Left for later:**
   - the design's step 3, the page engine (`page.export`);
   - step 5, the model plan's Python `create_*`;
   - the TeaVM unmodifiable-collections fix, the Compiler Rewrite line's, which the user rules on: a 200-class page's
     tab compile goes from 4.2 s to 73 ms with it.

## 2026-10-11 — TeaVM's unmodifiable set and map wrappers look up instead of scan: the tab boots in 0.3 s instead of 3.6 s (the Compiler Rewrite line)

The design is `docs/build-inventory/program/TEAVM_UNMODIFIABLE_DESIGN_2026_10_11.md`; the evidence
`docs/build-inventory/program/evidence/teavm-unmodifiable/`. The user ruled its §5 option 1, through the DataCube +
Python line's session ("lets get it all done"): the one-file port now; the TeaVM 0.16.0 bump stays a landing of its own (not L8, the upstream
Legend release's bump) and deletes the file. Branch `build/teavm-unmodifiable`. CI: run 38187695487 (every lane, every platform, as for a toolchain
change: the module is in several lanes), green on every job after one re-run of linux-arm / warehouse: the DataCube
line's `//datacube:python_engine_test` closed its browser page in its last case ("a widget message"), the same failure
as that line's own run 38175909649 before its landing, a race in the test that line is fixing; its 25 other cases,
among them the one that loads the changed module, passed first time. `//gates:local` green before (347 tests, twice:
on the landing and on its amendment after the audit); the lane query empty.

1. **The cause.** The DataCube line measured the tab compiling a 200-class page in 4.0 s (3,975 ms) where the native library
   takes 30 ms. An unobfuscated build of the module (its name section kept) named it: TeaVM 0.15.0's
   `Collections.unmodifiableSet` and `unmodifiableMap` override `iterator`, `size` and `remove` only, so `contains` and
   `get` fall to `TAbstractCollection`'s and `TAbstractMap`'s scans through the iterator. The compiler's universe of
   known names (`ModelNormalizer.resolveSynthesized`) sits in one such set, and `NameResolver` asks it per candidate name
   per package; the JDK's wrappers delegate, so the server never saw it. TeaVM fixed its own (master `5971683cf1`,
   2026-10-01; released in 0.16.0).
2. **What landed.** `third_party/teavm_classlib/src/org/teavm/classlib/java/util/TCollections.java`: TeaVM 0.15.0's
   file with that change ported (the set and the map wrappers answer `contains`, `containsAll`, `isEmpty`, `get`,
   `containsKey`, `containsValue` and `size` from the wrapped instance; the collection wrapper, which TeaVM has not
   changed and core uses nowhere, stays as 0.15.0's), with the package's notice header; the README row; the BUILD
   comment and the test selection; `PortedFromTest`'s list. No edit in `core/`, `tools/teavm/` or `wasm/`: the compiler
   stays as written, and the platform's library is held to the JDK's contract, as its number conversions already are.
3. **How it is held.** `TCollectionsTest` (JVM, `//third_party/teavm_classlib:tests`, the `core` lane): a counting set
   and a counting map, wrapped, answer every lookup right and open no iterator (against TeaVM's own file the same test
   fails: 7 iterators and 8 entry sets opened for the lookups), and `add`, `remove`, `clear`, `put` and both iterators'
   `remove` still refuse; the wrapper is a view, not a copy. The module: `//wasm:conformance_test`,
   `//wasm:differential_test`, `//wasm:round_trip_test`, and DataCube's, Studio's and Query's tests in the full run. No
   timing gate (CI's runners vary too much for one); the receipt is the DataCube line's rerun of
   `//datacube:model_scale_measure` on the landed module, added to the evidence README when it arrives.
4. **The numbers** (the production build run in Node; before is the DataCube line's
   `evidence/teavm-unmodifiable/before_obfuscated_node_datacube.jsonl`, after `after_fixed_node.jsonl`, both in the
   evidence README's table): a cold module loaded, booted and holding an empty model, 3,575 to 299 ms (the native
   library 101); the same holding a two-class model, 3,429 to 155; a warm module holding 1, 10, 50 and 200 classes,
   9, 131, 762 and 3,975 ms to 2, 4, 17 and 73 (native 0.7, 1.6, 6.0 and 30.0). The named build the profile ran on
   was a little slower before (3,618 and 4,239). The module: 5,093,390 to 5,093,779 bytes, the same for the measured
   port and the landed file (the collection wrapper's methods are unreachable from the planner and dropped).
5. **Not chased:** `Class.getEnumConstants` (2.5 % of the profile: TeaVM's `EnumSet` asks for the constants on every
   lookup) and the module's remaining 2.4x over the native library.

## 2026-10-11 — `#SQL{...}#`: a Postgres SELECT inside any Pure query, judged against Postgres 16 (the seventh line)

Announced in `docs/IN_FLIGHT.md` the same day (2aa74a8). Branch `claude/loving-euler-gjta59`; the study and the plan,
`docs/LEGEND_SQL_STUDY_2026_10_11.md` (§9 and §9.1 hold the numbers below).

1. **What lands.** A Postgres `SELECT` written as `#SQL{...}#` in a Pure query becomes an ordinary Relation expression.
   - **The reader and the translator:** a new package, `protocol/sql/`.
   - **The seam:** `compiler/spec/SqlIslands`, typed once by the Typer's island arm.
   - **What it reads:**
     - joins of every kind (ON, USING, NATURAL);
     - FROM subqueries and WITH; UNION, INTERSECT and EXCEPT;
     - subqueries in expressions, correlated to any level (IN, EXISTS, ANY/ALL, scalar);
     - window functions with ROWS and RANGE frames, and named windows;
     - a catalog of Postgres's scalar functions, the statistical aggregates, and casts.
   - **Semantics:** Postgres's three-valued logic is spelled out in the Pure itself (register S44). What has no
     faithful Pure spelling is refused by name, never approximated.
   - **Registered:** S43 to S47 in `docs/SEMANTICS_REGISTER.md`.
2. **Four lowering fixes in `lowering/Lowerer.java`.** The island's cases found them in plain Pure; each has a test
   that fails without its fix (`ConcatenateFlattenCheckerTest`, `CorrelatedRelationCheckerTest`):
   - A concatenate whose branch sorts or limits rendered `... LIMIT 2 UNION ALL ...`. Such a branch is now a
     subselect.
   - `exists` over a sliced relation (limit, offset, qualify) merged its predicate into the slice's WHERE, so it ran
     before the LIMIT. That was a silent wrong answer: `[1, 2]` for `[2]`. Such a relation is now isolated first.
   - A join condition read any variable but the left side's as the right side, so an enclosing row's `$p.id` became
     the right side's own `id`. An enclosing row now resolves through the enclosing scopes.
   - A relation `map` read as a value (`map->toOne`) did not push the enclosing row's scope, so a correlated one
     could not resolve. It now pushes it, as the `exists` and `size` arms do. The independent review found that
     this let a row's own column that a filter cannot fold in place (a window column) resolve to the enclosing
     row's same-named column, or fail at the query's root; a row's own variable is now never looked up among the
     enclosing rows (`scopedResolver`, two more tests).
3. **The parity corpus.** legend-engine 4.145.0's 1,703 `parity-tests` cases, plus 177 of legend-lite's own
   (`core/src/test/resources/sql-parity/lite/`), run as islands.
   - **Two lanes:** `//core:sql_parity_test` (DuckDB) and `//core:sql_parity_postgres_test` (Postgres 16), both in
     `//gates:core`.
   - **The judge:** Postgres 16's own answers, snapped. The Postgres lane checks each snapped answer against
     Postgres itself on every run.
   - **The ratchet:** each case's status is held by `ledger.tsv`.
   - **The result, identical in both lanes:**

     | | upstream's 1,703 | own 177 |
     |---|---|---|
     | PASS | 951 | 144 |
     | FAIL (wrong answer) | 0 | 0 |
     | BUG (answers what Postgres rejects) | 0 | 0 |
     | ERROR (errs where Postgres answers) | 0 | 0 |
     | REFUSED by name | 623 | 18 |
     | BOTH_ERROR | 61 | 15 |
     | SKIP | 68 | 0 |

   - **Against upstream:** upstream legend-engine passes 1,026 of its 1,703, with 36 wrong answers and 61 accepted
     invalid queries.
4. **Judges.**
   - **The local gate:** `bazel test --lockfile_mode=error //gates:local` on the branch merged with main e56d802: 332 targets, 316 pass. The 16 that fail are this root container's. 13 are browser and timeout targets that fail the same way on main's tree before this work (11283c8): a WebAssembly signature trap in three DataCube and Query harnesses, `//site:verify_test`'s selector wait, six tests that time out even alone, and a download from `extensions.duckdb.org`. The other 3 are the Postgres targets, which `initdb` refuses as root.
   - **The Postgres targets in a root container:** `//core:sql_parity_postgres_test`, `//core:sql_island_postgres_test`
     and `//core:postgres_arm_test` pass through the unprivileged wrapper (`tools/postgres/as_unprivileged.sh`,
     7c21e6d on `claude/great-wright-p6t5s1`).
   - **The six corpus passes,** rerun against a baseline built from main 8c8b92d the same day: 22 result files
     identical, 0 differing (`compare_judges.py`; both builds executed every pass, 31 sandboxed processes each,
     about 16 minutes). Rerun on 2026-10-12 with the review's `scopedResolver` fix: 0 differing again
     (the six passes executed, about 20 minutes).
   - **The full CI run:** the pull request's (neema2/legend-lite#28). It landed 2026-10-12 as ebc419f, merging d312dfd
     over main d2eefc5 with `[skip ci]`:
     - gates run 38198865199, green on every job (52 checks) after one re-run of windows / warehouse;
     - diagnostics run 38198865034, green.

     The re-run's failure was `//datacube:python_engine_test`'s teardown race, which this change does not touch: answers
     to a taken-down widget view were still in flight when the browser closed. Its first two runs failed only in the
     core lanes, in `//core:sql_parity_postgres_test`'s check that the snapped answers are Postgres's:
     - **Linux, macOS and Windows** (38194644588): the two `AGE(x)` answers drifted a day after their snap. `AGE(x)` is
       measured from today, and so is `CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '365 days'`: the three are now volatile, not snapped
       (SKIP; they were refused).
     - **macOS and Windows** (both runs): 13 `bytea` answers had been snapped as the JVM's identity hash of a byte
       array (`[B@2abf4075`), which repeats from run to run on Linux only; they are Postgres's `\x` hex now. And 15
       answers of Postgres's float functions (`cbrt`, `atan`, `log`, `cosh`, ...) differ in the last digit, because
       each platform's C library computes them: the check now lets two doubles differ by 1e-12 of the larger (the
       judge's own tolerance is 1e-6).
5. **Not done, recorded in the study** (§9.1, "Refused by name" and "Next steps"):
   - `round(x, n)`: Pure's round is half to even, Postgres's numeric round half away from zero.
   - `strpos`: Pure's `indexOf` is lowered one too high; PCT pins it.
   - `parseDecimal` lowers to a fixed `DECIMAL(5, 2)`.
   - LATERAL, intervals, arrays, JSON operators, regular expressions.

## 2026-10-12 — `#SQL{...}#`: the semi-structured step — jsonb over Variant, LATERAL, set-returning functions

Announced in `docs/IN_FLIGHT.md` the same day (d9adc5a). Branch `claude/loving-euler-gjta59`; the study,
`docs/LEGEND_SQL_STUDY_2026_10_11.md` §9.2 (what reads, what is refused, the findings, the numbers below).

1. **What lands.** A Variant column is Postgres's `jsonb` in the SQL front end (register S49).
   - **Navigation:** `->` and subscripts are `get`. `->>` is its text (`to(@String)`). `#>` and `#>>` walk a constant
     `text[]` path, as do `json(b)_extract_path(_text)`.
   - **Constants and casts:** `'...'::jsonb`, `jsonb '...'` and `text::jsonb` are `fromJson`. `to_jsonb` is `toVariant`.
   - **Set-returning functions,** in FROM, after a LATERAL, or as a whole select-list item:
     - `json(b)_array_elements(_text)` and `json(b)_object_keys`;
     - `generate_series` of integers (`range`);
     - `unnest(ARRAY[...])` and `unnest(string_to_array(...))` (`flatten`).
   - **LATERAL subqueries:** by comma, `CROSS JOIN` and `[INNER] JOIN ... ON`, each Pure's `lateral`.
   - **A query without FROM:** one row.
   - **Refused by name:** what lite would answer otherwise than Postgres (the study's list), e.g. `jsonb`'s order and
     equality as keys, `json(b)_array_length`, `LEFT JOIN LATERAL`, `WITH ORDINALITY`.
2. **Two fixes in `sql/dialect/`,** found by the cases, both in plain Pure:
   - **`DuckDb.java`:** `toMany(@Variant)` cast to `JSON[]`, which turns jsonb's null elements into SQL's NULL: a
     list read them as missing. It now reads an array's elements with `json_extract(x, '$[*]')`.
     `LowerRelationTest`'s two pins of that SQL changed with it. PCT's `testToManyFromNonArray` still holds.
   - **`Postgres.java`:** `toMany(@Variant)` and `to(@Map)` read a value of the wrong shape as an empty list or no
     map, where Postgres, Pure and DuckDB raise an error. They now raise Postgres's own.
3. **The parity corpus,** identical in both lanes (`//core:sql_parity_test`, `//core:sql_parity_postgres_test`):

   | | upstream's 1,703 | own 244 (177 before) |
   |---|---|---|
   | PASS | 1,016 (951 before) | 192 (144 before) |
   | FAIL, BUG, ERROR | 0 | 0 |
   | REFUSED by name | 558 | 30 |
   | BOTH_ERROR | 61 | 22 |
   | SKIP | 68 | 0 |

   The own cases are `lite/json.yaml` (41) and `lite/lateral.yaml` (26), new. The judge reads a `json` or `jsonb`
   cell as its JSON value, and the text of an object or array as JSON (S49).
4. **Judges,** on the branch rebased onto main c03ac6b (main's d9adc5a since, documentation only, merged in):
   - **core, checks, the PCT lanes:** `//core:core_tests`, `//gates:checks`, `//pct:pct_duckdb` and `//pct:pct_channel_b`: 169 of 169
     pass. Their first run found two red: `//core:guardrails` (four rules: the bare-name switch arms, the regex
     family, TeaVM's `isBlank`, SQL-shaped text) and `//core:update_generated_4_test` (the claim census named the
     translator for `fromJson`'s FQN). Each is held now without moving a pin (51ef576): the set-returning functions
     are a table, not name arms, and the translator calls `fromJson` by its simple name, as it does every native.
   - **The Postgres targets** (`//pct:pct_postgres`, `//core:sql_parity_postgres_test`,
     `//core:sql_island_postgres_test`, `//core:postgres_arm_test`), through the unprivileged wrapper: 8 of 8 pass.
   - **The six corpus passes,** against a baseline built from main d9adc5a: 0 result files differing
     (`compare_judges.py`). The branch changes core, which every pass reads, so with the disk cache off both builds
     executed all six.
   - **The full CI run:** the pull request's, neema2/legend-lite#33: run 38316829892 on fee1fd8 green on every job
     (Linux, macOS, Windows, linux-arm; "gates green"), as was the run on d774f93; merged as e647bf3.
5. **Not done, recorded in the study** (§9.2's open findings and its "Next steps"):

## 2026-10-12 — `#SQL{...}#`: the basics — filters, aggregates, functions, casts, dates, judged and fuzzed against Postgres

Announced in `docs/IN_FLIGHT.md` as the semi-structured step's widenings (5cb0ac1, aa0c469). Same branch
`claude/loving-euler-gjta59`; it lands in one pull request with the semi-structured step above. The study,
`docs/LEGEND_SQL_STUDY_2026_10_11.md` §9.3, says what reads, what is refused and why, and the numbers below.

1. **What lands.** The user's order: the basics first (filters, aggregations, joins, select lists, functions).
   - **Aggregates:** `FILTER (WHERE ...)`, `DISTINCT` in each, `string_agg(... ORDER BY ...)`, `bool_and`/`bool_or`/
     `every`, `percentile_cont`/`percentile_disc ... WITHIN GROUP`, `corr`/`covar_pop`/`covar_samp`; the boolean
     ones and the covariances also over a window.
   - **Windows:** `lag`/`lead` with a default (where the other row is outside the partition, never where its value
     is NULL).
   - **NULL and typing:** NULL constants typed as Postgres types them; comparisons with NULL, IN lists and BETWEEN in
     three-valued logic; CASE, COALESCE, GREATEST and LEAST resolved to one type; ceil, floor, sign, round, extract
     and date_part in Postgres's types.
   - **Functions:** exact integer division; `round(x, n)`/`trunc(x, n)` of a numeric exact; `substring`, `strpos`,
     `left`/`right` with negative counts, `power`; `concat` and `||` spellings.
   - **Casts:** integer and smallint ranges, a numeric rounded half away from zero, a double half to even,
     `varchar(n)`. Text values cast to numbers are refused (DuckDB reads `'1.5'`, `'1e3'`, `'1_000'`).
   - **Inexact numerics:** a quotient, average or root of numerics is a Float here and exact in Postgres; what
     rounds or spells one is refused (`floor(0.3 / 0.1)` is 3 there, 2 from the double), a double in it or not.
   - **A sum of integers** is a bigint or a numeric in Postgres by the column's width, which the translator does not
     know: dividing it by an integer is refused (`sum(x)::bigint / n` and `sum(x)::numeric / n` translate).
   - **Dates:** a date plus or minus days, the days between dates, interval constants (months, then days, then
     time), `make_date`, `make_timestamp`, `date_trunc` of a timestamp.
2. **Two fixes in `sql/dialect/`,** each announced in IN_FLIGHT, each with a test that fails without it:
   - **`RootNumericTypes.java`:** under DISTINCT, an ORDER BY key that is a projection cast to its numeric type is
     ordered by the cast expression (Postgres: "for SELECT DISTINCT, ORDER BY expressions must appear in select
     list").
   - **`QuantileOrder.java`:** DuckDB's descending discrete percentile at `p = 0` read element 0 of a 1-based list
     (NULL); it is the first value, as Pure's percentile and Postgres's `percentile_disc` say.
     `TypeInferenceIntegrationTest.testPercentile_GroupBy_Discrete_Descending_AtZero` pins it. Widened by the
     review (6d5f0e1): both orders compute the element as Postgres does, `ceil(p * N)` in double precision.
3. **The parity corpus,** identical in both lanes (`//core:sql_parity_test`, `//core:sql_parity_postgres_test`):

   | | upstream's 1,703 | own 381 (244 at the step above) |
   |---|---|---|
   | PASS | 1,122 (1,016 at the step above) | 284 |
   | FAIL, BUG, ERROR | 0 | 0 |
   | REFUSED by name | 452 | 46 |
   | BOTH_ERROR | 61 | 51 |
   | SKIP | 68 | 0 |

   New own cases: `lite/functions.yaml` (139 now), `lite/windows.yaml` (51), `lite/dates.yaml` (21, new).
4. **The randomized check.** A scratch generator (never committed) wrote type-correct Postgres queries over the
   parity schema and ran them through both lanes against Postgres: 13 seeds, about 6,300 queries, growing with each
   feature. Each wrong answer it found is fixed and pinned by a case (the study lists them); the last seeds found
   none. One error remains by design: a product beyond the 38-digit decimal overflows where Postgres's numeric
   answers.
5. **Judges,** on the branch with main cbd8f01 merged in (main's changes since the step above are IN_FLIGHT only):
   - **core, checks, the PCT lanes:** `//core:core_tests`, `//gates:checks`, `//pct:pct_duckdb`,
     `//pct:pct_channel_b`: 169 of 169 pass on every commit of the step. Guard findings on the way were held without
     moving a pin: name arms became set lookups, `rowMapper` is called by its simple name (the claim census), a
     regex split became a scan, a `HashMap` an unmodifiable `LinkedHashMap`.
   - **The Postgres targets** (`//pct:pct_postgres`, `//core:sql_parity_postgres_test`,
     `//core:sql_island_postgres_test`, `//core:postgres_arm_test`), through the unprivileged wrapper: 8 of 8 pass.
   - **The six corpus passes,** against a baseline built from main cbd8f01: 0 result files differing (`compare_judges.py`); with the disk cache off both builds executed all six.
   - **The full CI run:** the pull request's, neema2/legend-lite#33: run 38316829892 on fee1fd8 green on every job
     (Linux, macOS, Windows, linux-arm; "gates green"), as was the run on d774f93; merged as e647bf3.
   - **The independent review** (an agent that wrote none of it): eight wrong answers traced, each measured, fixed and
     pinned (the study's §9.3 lists them); three recorded (a constant column's `corr` noise in Postgres, inexact
     comparisons at the exact boundary, `make_date` of year 0).
6. **Not done, recorded in the study:** regular expressions (`~`, `regexp_*`); `mode()` (DuckDB breaks ties
   otherwise); `corr` over a window; text cast to a number; intervals as values and timestamp differences; the
   semi-structured step's open findings (DuckDB's JSON numbers as doubles among them, for the user to decide).

## 2026-10-12 — A stored Variant column leaves the statement as JSON, whatever the shape of the query (the Compiler Rewrite line)

The design is `docs/VARIANT_STORAGE_CENSUS_2026_09_27.md` (the user's "go", 2026-09-27), its "Addendum 2026-10-12: the
star egress" this landing adds. The finding is the DataCube line's (2026-10-12), probed on Python's DuckDB and the tab's
alike; the Plan Gen / Exec Split line agreed with the placement (lowering only; result typing may assume JSON for a
Variant output in every shape) and asked for the statement's own column type to be held, which the test does. Branch
`core/variant-star-egress`; the announcement cbd8f014f on `main` first; rebased onto main 36b72ee13 (PRs #31 and #33 in)
before landing, the core change byte-identical (the two patches compared line for line), and the judges, the render
census, the local gate and one CI run re-run on the rebased tree. CI: run 38327604817 on the rebased branch, green on
all 50 jobs first time (the summary job a dispatched run skips); the first run, 38310588988 on the commit before the
rebase, green on all 50 too; main's own push run on the landing, 38331688457, green (every lane, every platform; `core`
is where the test runs, and the module in `wasm` and DataCube's tests plan through the same renderer). `//gates:local`
green (348 pass, 2 skipped: `//tools/guards:classpath_test` and `markdown_inputs_test`, which depend on the MariaDB
lane, incompatible on this Mac tests); the lane query empty; the judges against baselines built from main 36b72ee13:
every result file the same (0 of 23 differ;
`docs/build-inventory/program/evidence/variant-star-egress/judges_compare.txt`); the render census: 55,016 entries, 41
differ, every one in the core lane's own unit tests: the new test's renders, and seven `extend` shapes over a table
holding a Variant column now listing their columns, each with its successor (`render_census_compare.txt` beside it; the
audit is `AUDIT.md` there).

1. **The cause.** V2 of the census reads a stored Variant column as JSON through the DuckDB dialect's `columnRef`
   hook, `CAST(col AS JSON)` on a column REFERENCE. A star renders none: a star frame (`SELECT *`, which a bare
   source, `limit`, `filter`, `sort` and `distinct` keep to the statement's end) and a star projection
   (`SELECT t0.*, x`: `extend`) alike. So an uploaded JSON file's `customer` column, a STRUCT as DuckDB's `read_json`
   stores it and a Variant to the model, left the query as `{"name":"A","tier":2}` under `select` and as the
   STRUCT under `limit`, and each executor rendered the STRUCT its own way (the tab's reader quoted the nested
   integer). D2 of the census ("a whole column value leaving the query") was removed for projections, not for stars;
   the census's own test projected and grouped and never took a bare `limit`.
2. **What landed.** `core/src/main/java/com/legend/sql/dialect/VariantEgress.java`, a DuckDB render pass on the
   statement root only (the renderer's `rewriteRoot` hook, last of the dialect's passes; `StoredReads` follows):
   every star standing for a source that holds a stored Variant column is spelled into that source's columns
   (`Stars.columns`, as `StoredReads` spells a star over a read table), the Variant ones read through the hook
   (`CAST(t0.V AS JSON) AS V`), every other a bare reference, a join's sides each in place; a UNION's branches and a
   WITH's body are roots too (`RootNumericTypes`'s precedent). Below the root nothing changes (a star there feeds a
   reference the hook already reads); no other dialect changes (native nested storage is DuckDB's); the wire wrappers
   (`_wire0`, the JSON and CSV wires) already read through references and are unchanged. `DuckDb.storedVariant` over
   an output column; the pass added last in `DuckDb.passes()`.
3. **How it is held.** `LowerRelationTest.wholeVariantReadsAsJsonInEveryShape` (`//core:core_tests_lowering`, the
   `core` lane): ten shapes (bare, sort and limit, filter, sort, distinct, select, extend, join, a sorted join,
   concatenate) over one column held three ways (JSON text in a VARCHAR, DuckDB JSON, a native STRUCT): the read in
   the SQL (`CAST(t0.V AS JSON) AS V`, and in each UNION branch), the statement's own column type `JSON` as DuckDB's
   JDBC reports it (what a result decoder sees), identical rows across the storages. Without the pass the JSON-type
   check and the row comparison fail for the VARCHAR and STRUCT storages. The judges, the render census and the
   corpora show no other SQL text changed: no pinned text anywhere has a root star over a DuckDB Variant column.
4. **The audit** (the branch's, before landing): one blocker, the star projections (`extend`'s `SELECT t0.*, x`,
   `ExistsJoinForm`'s, `Pivots`' `StarExcept`), which the first cut's star-frame-only rule missed; three should-fix:
   UNION and WITH roots, the first cut's join wrapper dropping the frame's ORDER BY from the outermost statement
   (gone with the wrapper: a join's sides are listed in place), and the test's coverage; three nits (a comment, line
   lengths). All taken.
5. **Not chased.** `Fold.declaredKindEnvelope`'s Float rule still rides a star frame through unchanged (its own
   2026-09-17 reason: a wire already DOUBLE); it is a different rule and untouched. The tab's reader's JSON rendering
   of a STRUCT that reaches it by another route (the DataCube line's `toScalar` fix) stands on its own.

## 2026-10-12 — One `DUCKDB_PLATFORMS`: DuckDB's spelling of our platform names, in one place (the Compiler Rewrite line)

A Bazel-only tidy-up after the DataCube line's PR #31: its httpfs extension (step 2b) brought a second hand-spelled copy
of the mapping from our platform names (`//tools/platforms`) to the names DuckDB publishes its extensions under --
`python/BUILD.bazel`'s `_DUCKDB_PLATFORMS` beside `warehouse/defs.bzl`'s five literal `POSTGRES_EXTENSION` labels. Now
one constant, `DUCKDB_PLATFORMS` in `tools/platforms/defs.bzl`, read by both: the five httpfs `java_run` targets and the
`platform_select` behind `//python:wheel_duckdb`, and the postgres extension's select. No behaviour change: the same
five repositories (`MODULE.bazel`'s `duckdb_*_extension_<name>`) on the same five platforms, the same
`target_compatible_with`. Left alone on purpose: the JDBC jar's library names (`warehouse/BUILD.bazel`, both macOS

## 2026-10-14 — `#IQ{...}#`: the first landing — SAP IQ SQL inside any Pure query, judged against SQL Anywhere 17 (the tenth line)

Announced in `docs/IN_FLIGHT.md` ("A tenth line", 987c37e18). Branch `claude/iq-island-1`: four commits over main
941f8382d (5c977f4bf the study and the oracle, 27e1e4dbf the seam, 9fb52c67e the island, 9ba06c4ad the rest of M0 and
the reviews' fixes), built on `claude/iq-island` and rebased. The study, `docs/IQ_SQL_STUDY_2026_10_13.md` (§9.1 holds
what reads, what is refused and why, the reviews' findings and the numbers below).

1. **What lands.** A query written for SAP IQ 16.2 as `#IQ{...}#`, or `#IQ:<profile>{...}#` for one of five closed
   profiles, becomes an ordinary Relation expression that returns IQ's answer.

## 2026-10-14 — The three planner defects the tenth line found: integer folds beyond long, an all-NULL CASE in the stamp census, a union's column stamps (the Compiler Rewrite line)

The tenth line (the `#IQ{...}#` island) reported three planner defects to this line in IN_FLIGHT ("The compiler and
stamp program"). Branch `core/iq-finds`, three commits over afd07af19 (d619c5cd6 at the head on main); the audit
(`docs/build-inventory/program/evidence/iq-finds/AUDIT.md`): no blocker, two should-fixes and four nits, all taken
before the commits were rewritten.

1. **Integer folds beyond long.** The parser keeps a literal beyond long a `BigInteger`, and every fold over two spelled
integers read `longValue()`, which wraps it: `LiteralUnroll.nativeFold`'s `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` (`99999999999999999999 >
9223372036854775807` folded to false, and `$x > ...` with `$x` let-bound to it is the same fold after inlining),
`NormalizeFolds`' `eq`/`equal` on inlined bodies, and -- the audit's find, the main path -- `LiteralUnroll.literal`,
whose spelled-integer `Scalar` drives the inliner's equality fold, `contains`, `in`, a map's `get` and groupBy keys (two
different literals beyond long folded equal, two groupBy keys merged). All read `TypedCInteger.big()`, the exact value.
`ExactIntegerFoldTest` pins the compares and both equality paths through the typer's own overloads. The remaining
`longValue()` reads of a spelled integer (an index, an offset, a precision: `at(2^64)` picks element 0) are PARK-37 in
the ledger, anchored on the `at()` read.

2. **An all-NULL CASE in the stamp census.** `StampCensus.check` exempted a bare NULL as shape-ambiguous (SQL NULL
carries pure's EMPTY in scalar and list positions), but `listShaped` counted a CASE whose every branch is NULL as a
list, so such a CASE under a scalar stamp fired the invariant. The exemption is `nullOnly`: a NULL, or a CASE of
NULL-only branches (no ELSE being SQL's NULL); a CASE with a real list branch still fires (`StampCensusTest`). The
auditor's older gap stays as placed: a no-ELSE CASE of list branches never fired and still does not.

3. **A union's column stamps.** `ConcatenateChecker.positional` carried the left operand's schema as the union's, stamps
included, so a NULL-constant first branch (`[]->cast(@String)`, the islands' spelling, [0..0]) stamped the united column
always-empty and an enclosing test of it folded away (no row found, a size-0 error, a random sort key).
`TypedConcatenate.unionInfo(left, right, m)` is the one place a relation concatenate's info comes from: the left's
carrier, names and types, each common column's stamp `Multiplicity.union` of the two sides'. The typer's two builders
and the resolver's five rebuilds (`ImportDataFlowAppend`, `DriverPkAppend`, `StoreResolver`, `StackBuilder`,
`SyntheticHeads`: the audit's second find, each took one side's info) take it; `ClassConcatenates` keeps its
schema-equal union and the class-collection overload's own info. `TypeCheckerTest` pins [0..1] on either side, [0..0]
for two empty branches, [1] for two value branches.

**Judges.** The six corpus passes against baselines built from main afd07af19 the same day: 0 of 23 result files differ
(`docs/build-inventory/program/evidence/iq-finds/judges_compare.txt`); the render census, main's tree against the
branch: 55,747 entries, 0 differ (`render_census_compare.txt` beside it); `//spec:reference_lane` and `//core:census`
green; `//gates:local` 363 pass, 2 skipped (the two guards incompatible on this Mac); the lane query empty. CI: run
38605839662 on the branch, every lane, every platform, green on all 50 jobs, the Windows Postgres PCT job on its re-run
(its first try failed to build the test launcher when the runner's query of the remote cache failed, no test having
run); main's own run on the landing, 38611525856, green on every job.

## 2026-10-14 — A computed column reads the enclosing row: a correlated subquery's select list no longer throws at the lowering (the Compiler Rewrite line)

The tenth line (the `#IQ{...}#` island), compiling real-world queries, reported in IN_FLIGHT that a correlated scalar
subquery whose select list reads the outer row inside an expression (`SELECT max(x.age) + e.ID FROM ... x` under `FROM
... e`; both islands reach it) threw `IllegalStateException` "unresolvable even after isolation" at
`Lowerer.computedColumns`, while the same read in the subquery's WHERE worked. Branch `core/correlated-columns`, one
commit over cafedc562 (9bc695885 at the head on main); the audit
(`docs/build-inventory/program/evidence/correlated-columns/AUDIT.md`): see its verdict there.

**The cause and the fix.** `tryComputedColumns` lowered a column lambda's body with a resolver that ignored the variable
read and resolved every name against the base select: an enclosing row's column was unfoldable (isolate once, then
loud), and one named like a base column would have resolved to the base's, silently. Predicates never had this:
`tryPredicate` resolves through `scopedResolver`, the lambda's own row against the select and any other variable through
the `enclosing` stack every scalar-subquery arm pushes, never the select's same-named column. Computed columns now take
the same resolver (one line of `Lowerer`). `CorrelatedComputedColumnTest` pins the `#SQL{...}#` spellings end to end on
DuckDB against the database's own answer to the same SQL (no snap), the plain-Pure spelling (an `extend` over a nested
relation reading the outer row, under a `groupBy` and without), and a same-named column resolving to the enclosing row.

**Judges.** The six corpus passes against baselines built from main cafedc562 the same day: 0 of 23 result files differ
(`docs/build-inventory/program/evidence/correlated-columns/judges_compare.txt`); the render census, main's tree against
the branch: 58,688 entries, 6 differ, all six the new test class's own renders (before 0, after 1), no existing
statement changed (`render_census_compare.txt` beside it); `//spec:reference_lane` and `//core:census` green;
`//gates:local` 363 pass, 2 skipped (the two guards incompatible on this Mac); the lane query empty. CI: run 38626481778
on the branch, every lane, every platform, green on all 50 jobs first time; main's own run on the landing, 38631500150,
green on every job.

1. **The stress corpus** (`core/src/test/resources/sql-stress/`, the user: "an insane sql corpus that stress tests our
   parser and sqlgen"): 86 queries, each scaled along one axis (joins of 2 to 50 tables, FROM nesting to 50, IN and
   EXISTS to 30, 50 scalar subqueries, CTE chains, 40 set operations, CASE, OR, `+` and parentheses to 2,000, 500
   columns, 50 windows, nested casts to 100, combined monsters), each run raw on Postgres 16 and as an island on both
   lanes, planned, timed, measured and judged (`testcases/SqlStress.java`, `run.sh`). `baseline.tsv` is main before
   the fixes, `after.tsv` this branch; the README tabulates both. No query that finished gave an answer other than
   Postgres's, before or after; eleven that timed out or overflowed now pass; none got worse.
2. **The fixes, measured by it:**
   - `compiler/spec/JoinChecker.java` (cross-area): a join's inputs are typed again only when its condition reads a
     column by name (`readsByName`, `rowRead`): a chain of N joins typed its innermost input 2^N times (20 tables:
     36 s to plan; now 0.45 s; 50 tables: 0.9 s). Pinned by `JoinCheckerTest.aLongJoinChainTypesEachInputOnce` (40
     modern-condition joins, in the core suite, its own timeout: the compiler line's ask 3).
   - `protocol/sql/SqlToPure.java`: a strict operation merges a strict operand's NULL test into its own when that
     operand is the one that may be NULL (a 10-term `+` chain was 96 KB of SQL, now 253 characters); AND and OR
     chains read without recursion and combined as a balanced tree (a 500-term OR overflowed a default stack),
     reachable by a dialect as `At.logical` (the tenth line takes it for `#IQ`); an integer cast of a value an
     enclosed cast already holds to the range is not tested again (ten nested casts were 9 MB of SQL, now 327
     characters at any depth); `PostgresDialect`'s default name of a cast read once a level (2^n).
3. **The planner's wrong answers** (the tenth line found three through `#SQL`; the review one more), wrong for plain
   Pure too, each pinned by a DuckDB integration test that fails without its fix and by unit tests beside the method
   (`FoldTest.aKeylessAggregateIsABoundary`, `NullSemanticsTest.emptyColumnsAreEqual`: ask 2):
   - `lowering/Fold.java`, `SubselectPrune.java`, `RelationPredicates.java`: an aggregate with no GROUP BY is a

## 2026-10-15 — The compiler's two scale costs: a join's outputs computed once, a fold budget for written projections; the census tool lowers with the storeless runtime (the Compiler Rewrite line)

The tenth line's scale suite (IN_FLIGHT, 2026-10-14; 650 points over 75 query shapes) measured two walls in the
compiler's files: a chain of 100 joins planned in about a second and 250 in 27-40 s, and 20 nested derived tables gave
53 MB of SQL. Branch `core/scale-costs`, one commit over 8d2e55a65 (487a0f460 at the head on main); the audit
(`docs/build-inventory/program/evidence/scale-costs/AUDIT.md`): see its verdict there. The measurements before and
after, and the program that took them, are in `measurements.txt` and `ScratchScale.java.txt` beside it.

**A join's outputs, once.** `SqlSource.Join.outputs()` built both sides' column lists on every call, and a left-deep
chain of N joins built them N levels deep each time a column was looked up (`Fold.sourceColumn` asks more than once per
read), so planning grew faster than the cube of the chain. The join now computes its delivered columns when it is made
(a record component its four-argument constructor fills) and every reader gets that list. Measured on `#SQL{...}#`
chains over one table, before and after: 100 joins 575 to 158 ms, 150 joins 1,915 to 214 ms, 200 joins 3,099 to 314 ms,
250 joins 8,770 to 434 ms, 100 comma joins 2,390 to 112 ms; the SQL the same.

**A fold budget.** A fold writes a computed projection's expression in the place of each read of it
(`Fold.resolveIntoExact`), so a column read twice doubled at every level of nesting: 10 nested derived tables reading
the level below twice gave 7 MB of SQL, 15 ran out of memory after 168 s. The rule is Calcite-shaped (ProjectMergeRule's
`bloat`, its default 100): one pass, a project's or extend's columns or a filter's predicate, may grow its select by at
most 100 expression nodes through such writes; the first write of each projection is free (an extend's kept projection
is that write, the audit's find: a chain of extends each adding the two columns before it grew as Fibonacci's numbers
until it was charged), every further write costs the growth it brings; past the budget the read is unfoldable, the pass
isolates its base and the reads go through the subselect, as every unfoldable read does (`Fold.Budget`, spent by
`scopedResolver`'s own-row reads). A plain column costs nothing, so renames and small chains fold as before. A read made
on an enclosing row's behalf (a correlated subquery's) spends no budget: it is written once in its subquery, and a
refusal there would fail the inner pass, whose isolation cannot change the outer row; a whole-variable read spends none
either (isolation could not cure its refusal); a graph fetch's row resolver, no fold pass's, takes an unbounded budget.
Measured after: 10 levels 1,794 chars, 20 levels 3,814 chars, each planned in under 30 ms.

**The census tool.** `tools/census/RenderCensus.java` lowered with no runtime, which the planner refuses since PR #39
(decision D2: the language of raw text is the runtime's database), so every case failed on both sides of a comparison
(the stress line found it and ran a copy); it now lowers with the storeless runtime on DuckDB declared beside the model
(`StorelessRuntime.with`; a model that declares it keeps its own).

**Judges.** `ScaleCostsTest` pins the work, not seconds (a join's outputs are one list; a chain of a hundred joins
lowers; twelve doubling levels read the base column four times, the null-safe sum reading each operand twice so the
budget isolates every second level, and the answer is DuckDB's own across the isolation; twenty levels of the extend
chain read it 44 times, all in the innermost select; a small computed column read twice still folds into one select).
The six corpus passes against baselines built from main 8d2e55a65 the same day: 0 of 23 result files differ
(`docs/build-inventory/program/evidence/scale-costs/judges_compare.txt`); the render census, main's tree against the
branch: 58,794 entries, 22 differ (`render_census_compare.txt` beside it: six the new test's own renders, and four cases
of the tenth line's IQ parity suite on each of DuckDB and Postgres, where an overflow-checked computed column read more
than once is now a subselect's, both parity tests passing with the same answers); the judges and the census ran on the
tree before two test-only edits (the parse door, the ledger pins), the local gate on the final tree;
`//spec:reference_lane` and `//core:census` green; `//gates:local` 364 pass, 2 skipped (the two guards incompatible on
this Mac); the lane query empty. CI: run 38689728911 on the branch, every lane, every platform, green on all 50 jobs
first time (the gates-green summary skipped, as on every dispatch); main's own run on the landing, 38693372933, red on
two jobs, neither this landing's: the macOS datacube job's runner was lost by GitHub (its annotation "The hosted runner
lost communication with the server"; no log; the same SHA green on the branch run), and the Windows core job timed out
`//core:core_tests_integration` at 300 s, as main's run 38667214956 on 10bc6fbe2 (PR #41, before this landing) had at
305.8 s; on Linux the suite's summed test time FELL with this landing, 153.8 s to 106.7 s, and on Windows the lane runs
it two to three times slower than it runs alone (the seventh line's diagnosis, PR #44: CPU contention beside the other
42 tests' JVMs, no I/O cost), a margin of the lane that predates this landing, which the seventh line is fixing and the
Bazel program reviews (the Phase 8 brief's "sharding; third order" item); the reading, with five runs' class times:

## 2026-10-22 — PCT on the clouds: channel A's plans run on the suite's held session, not a session-mode system one

The BigQuery lane measured channel A at 78bd5da3 against the merge-base: essential 615 s against 256 s, standard 567 s
against 237 s, relation 381 s against 215 s. A proxy over every connection the harness opens put all of it inside
BigQuery. Planning and the harness took the same time at both, and the statement counts were nearly equal (essential
815 and 836). Each query took twice as long (median 216 ms against 514 ms, the same for statements under 1,000
characters).

The cause is the connection. Since eee1e560 a cloud's plans whose session statements are its dialect's options alone
ran on one held SYSTEM session (`openSystem`). BigQuery's system connection adds `EnableSession`, which its temporary
tables need. On it the same `SELECT 1` takes 421 ms against 216 ms on the plain session (sixteen interleaved runs
each). The merge-base ran every case on the suite's plain session (`CloudLane.connect`).

Such a plan now runs on that session again: `TestBackend.held()`, a cloud's `open()`, replaces `heldSystem()`. A plan
that makes a table of the session's own (the system metamodel store) still runs on a new system session, as before.
A server lane still opens a session per plan.

The mixed-number statements were not BigQuery's cause: about 20 s at head, against a 334 s and a 283 s difference.

BEING MEASURED: channel A's timings on BigQuery, Snowflake and Databricks at this commit. Local: //pct:pct_discipline,
//core:core_tests_root and //core:core_tests_architecture green; the three clouds' PCT targets build.

## 2026-10-20 — Object identity: the audit's fixes (no silent identity, typed reads, a map flattens by multiplicity)

The user, 2026-10-20, on the branch's audit ("Yes fix all those"), and the merge gate: channel B green on every lane.

**Landed:**
- **No identity answers from an id the product does not track** (docs/OBJECT_IDENTITY_2026_10_20.md §4, register
  S104). Where the evaluations are not tracked, the plan path mints no id (`Lowerer.objectId`) and reading the object's
  identity raises by name in the database (`CanonicalRenderSql.trackedId`: every identity comparison, `toString`'s
  `@_` name, a key canon's JSON-carried object): an object the resolver builds from a store's rows (one construction
  for every row), one built in a lambda of a fold the database runs (`UserCallInliner.finish`), and a lambda body's let
  read inside a nested lambda or, where its value holds a lambda, read more than once (`SourceSubst.untrackedLetNodes`,
  marked where the typer folds the body). Before, each answered silently from a shared id.
- **A lambda body's let read at one level is one evaluation**: the let is spliced into its uses before typing, so
  each use was its own call (`[1, 2]->map(i | let a = mk(); $a == $a)` answered false; Pure true). A user call keeps
  the source node it was read from (`TypedUserCall.origin`, stamped by `Typer`), and the inliner instantiates a call
  once per source node at a point of its frame (`UserCallInliner.instantiated(call, ...)`).
- **The legacy verdict lane reads map positions** for its ids, as the plan path does (`Lowerer.iterating`).
- **`StructGet` and `ArrayLit` keep a type they are given** where their parts prove none (`SqlExpr`; `withChildren`
  carries it, as `Lambda`'s did), so MariaDB's one-field-struct workaround for a fold accumulator's list field
  (94a55a24) is deleted: the field read is typed as the column it replaces.
- **A map flattens by its mapper body's multiplicity** (`ListEncodings.lowerMap`), not by the SQL type of the body
  (which missed an untyped body and would flatten a `List<T>[1]`, one object that is an array in SQL).
- Register rows **S81** and **S82** removed (both differences are gone: testConcatenateTypeInference and
  testLetChainedWithAnotherFunction pass on every lane measured since 2026-10-20).
- Reviewed and kept, with reasons: Postgres writes an empty list arm of a coalesce as `'{}'` (Postgres types it from
  the other arms; `json[]` and `jsonb[]` are one SQL type here, and a jsonb canon would reorder the keys of every JSON
  object Postgres builds); a class with no properties carries `__type` (the layout's, from before the branch: an empty
  struct is no SQL value); the ledgers' short fragment pins (the expected side holds the reference interpreter's
  per-run ids).
- Found, not changed (a lowering defect of its own, loud): a fold the database runs whose accumulator is a list of
  objects built from other elements does not lower on DuckDB.

**Measured** (this container, 2be571ec less its ClickHouse decode arm, which the run below did not compile):
`ObjectIdentityTest` (the let cases and `anUntrackedObjectsIdentityIsRefusedByName`); `//core:core_tests` (25
targets); `//pct:pct_duckdb` 5 of 5 and `//pct:pct_channel_b` 5 of 5; `//spec:corpus_duckdb` and `//spec:corpus_h2`
exact; `//pct:pct_mariadb_{essential,grammar}` and `//pct:pct_mysql_essential` exact with the typed reads. Channel B
on MariaDB, MySQL, ClickHouse and Trino is red against the merge-base (the lane sessions' test-by-test diffs of
31196a87 against 59b547a5e4, main identical to the merge-base on every lane): the next entry fixes what the branch
broke there.

## 2026-10-20 — Object identity, steps 1 and 2: every object carries its evaluation; a map flattens its mapper's lists

The program: `docs/OBJECT_IDENTITY_2026_10_20.md` (the user's ruling of 2026-10-20, "lets fix identity properly"),
inside the plan-route parity work on DuckDB (`docs/PLAN_PATH_PROGRAM_2026_10_17.md` §9).

**Landed:**
- **Every object carries `__id` and `__type` on every lane** (`ClassLayouts.objectLayoutOf`, the identity layout
  without `__canon`; `Lowerer.withObjectIdentity`, armed on the plan path in `TypedQuery` and `Compiler.lower`), and no
  output shows them (`MixedEncoding.declaredOnly` at the JSON, variant and text writers). `removeDuplicates` on objects
  is `InstanceEquality`'s (a keyed class by its keys, a keyless class by its id).
- **The id is the construction's evaluation** (`compiler/spec/typed/Evaluation`, design §3.2): its source node
  (`NewChecker`), the instantiations around it (`UserCallInliner.reached`: each call inlined, each lambda applied, each
  spelled element unrolled; a let's value stamped where it is bound), a lambda's body completed where the lambda stands
  (`UserCallInliner.finish`), and the position of the element of each map it is built in (`Lowerer.objectId`,
  `Lowerer.iterating`: the mapper takes the 1-based position as its second parameter, which every dialect's
  `list_transform` takes; `SqlTyping` types that form). A site is a value (origin and path), so the statement executor's
  one inliner run per statement gives a let's object the same id in every statement (`ObjectSites`,
  `exec.InstanceIds`). Measured first: a site per tree node gave `mk() == mk()` true, two objects for a let read twice
  in a lambda's body (spliced before typing), and a let built outside a map its positions.
- **A map flattens a mapper whose value is a list** (`ListEncodings.map`): `[1, 2]->map(i | [3, 4]->map(j | $i + $j))`
  had two elements, `$qs->map(q | $q.xs)` a list of lists; the flatten read only a spelled collection.
- Where the product's identity is not yet Pure's: register **S104** (an object per relation row refused by name; a store
  row's object one id per construction; a fold's accumulator; a lambda's let read in a nested map).

## 2026-10-20 — The parity phase, second batch: twenty-five lane pins removed, ClickHouse's clamped dates refused by name

The program: `docs/PLAN_PATH_PROGRAM_2026_10_17.md` §9, the user's order of 2026-10-20 (PCT parity on every backend);
the first batch's next items.

**Fixed, each at its cause:**
- **Jaro-Winkler on MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite** (`MariaDb.jaroWinkler`, `SQLite.jaroWinkler`): a recursive walk over
  the second text matching each character to the first unmatched equal one of the first text inside the window, a
  second walk counting the matched characters out of order, the similarity and its prefix boost in DOUBLE (REAL)
  arithmetic, measured bit-equal to DuckDB's `jaro_winkler_similarity` (Postgres's walk, spelled without LATERAL and
  `generate_series`, which these have none of). MariaDB's recursive CTE reads no outer column, so texts that read a
  row stay a wall there, by name, as its edit distance's. Six pins.
- **MongoDB's dynamic pivot through the probe plan** (the keyed plan of 2026-10-20 on its tenth database): a
  parameter marker is bound by its place among the markers, as SQL's `?` (`{"$legendParam": "?"}`; a per-key region's
  copies are copies of its text, so an index written in it would be stale in every copy after the first); a key's
  cell binds through that marker (`SqlWriter.bindKey`); the group stage's per-key aggregates and the projection's
  per-key columns are per-key regions, each field named by the key's position (`MongoDb.GroupField`,
  `MongoDbPipeline.group`/`projection`); a star with excluded columns is the row with those fields unset
  (`$unsetField`, the composite key's source); the keys and the body are two commands with no transaction across
  them (`KeysSnapshot.NONE`, register S103) and no column limit (a document's 16 MB is). The plan carries the names
  each statement writes its cells under (`ExecutionPlan.Keyed.keyFields`, each output's `field`, a per-key cell's
  `_pk<position>_<field>`; plan JSON v9), which a session reading by name needs and JDBC, reading by place, ignores.
  Ten pins.
- **MongoDB's divide answers a double** (`{"$divide": [{"$toDouble": a}, {"$toDouble": b}]}`), as every dialect's:
  `$divide` kept two Decimal128s' 34 digits. `testDecimalDivide`.
- **The metamodel's tables inline where a database has no temporary table** (`SqlDialect.temporaryTables`,
  `PlanMaker.inlineRows`; Trino and MongoDB): each table the query reads is its own rows, each cell its column's
  typed literal (the graph's facts, plan-time constants), a table of no rows a select of typed NULLs holding none.
  `testBasic` on both (`PlanMakerTest` pins the form: no session table, the statement's VALUES).
- **MD5, SHA-1 and SHA-256 written in SQLite's SQL** (`SqliteDigests`, new): the text's UTF-8 bytes padded as each
  digest pads them, one walk building each chunk's words (and the SHAs' schedule), one walk running the rounds, the
  32-bit arithmetic in SQLite's integers (no XOR there: `(x | y) & ~(x & y)`); measured bit-equal to the JDK's on 13
  texts of 0 to 200 characters, multi-byte UTF-8 among them; about 6 to 9 KB of SQL each. `hashCode` is MariaDB's and
  Postgres's construction over it (the first 64 bits of the MD5 of the values' text as a JSON array, read signed).
  Five pins.
- **ClickHouse: a LEFT join's condition both sides read, no equality** (`OuterJoinResidualsAsMatches`, new):
  ClickHouse keeps none under `join_use_nulls` ("contains column from left and right table", measured 25.8), and its
  INNER join keeps one, so the condition's matches come first (each distinct tuple of the left columns it reads,
  INNER-joined to the right side), then the left side LEFT-joined to them on that tuple, null-safe, the right
  alias naming the matches; a null-safe key between a join's sides is `isNotDistinctFrom` in its ON (its coalesce
  spelling is a residual, and an outer join needs a key). `testNestedJoinArithmeticComparisonExpression` (the engine
  passes it on ClickHouse); channel B Relation 461 -> 462, its floor raised with the reason.
- **ClickHouse's date arithmetic past its years raises by name** (`ClickHouse.outsideDates`): ClickHouse clamps a date
  past 1900 to 2299 to the end it passed (step 9 recorded `adjust` by a large count answering 2299-12-31, a silent
  wrong answer); the date the arithmetic reaches is checked first, in Int128 (a calendar unit by its year, any other
  by its microseconds since the epoch), and raised outside them, as MariaDB's "a date past the year 9999". The six
  `*BigNumber` adjust pins re-recorded with the refusal.

**Per lane, pins removed:** MongoDB 12, SQLite 7, MySQL 2, MariaDB 2, Trino 1, ClickHouse 1; re-recorded: ClickHouse's
six big-number adjusts.

**Named for later** (each measured, none moved): a Variant's key order on MySQL (its JSON type sorts an object's keys,
and its compaction is a cast to JSON) and on Postgres (jsonb's), three and two pins, a carrier change across every
variant test there; a named time zone where the database has no zone rules (MySQL and MariaDB without their zone
tables, SQLite), three pins, a design question put to the user (the zone's transitions as plan-time constants from

JSON (nineteen, the engine's own failures); `currentUserId` where the database names no user (SQLite, MongoDB).

**Channel B pins moved, each with its reason** (`ChannelBLane.PINS`): ClickHouse Relation 461 -> 462 (the join);
SQLite Standard 203 -> 205 and Unclassified 87 -> 92, MariaDB and MySQL Unclassified 91 -> 93 (as measured: the
digests, `hashCode`, Jaro-Winkler); Trino Grammar 131 -> 136 as measured, its wire bugs 0 -> 1 (channel A reads the

## 2026-10-20 — The parity phase, first batch: fifty-two lane pins removed at their causes, four re-recorded as the database's own

The program: `docs/PLAN_PATH_PROGRAM_2026_10_17.md` §9, the user's order of 2026-10-20 ("before we move on we need to
have 100% parity on PCT across all backends"). The triage (every pin of the 42 channel-A ledgers against legend-engine
4.145.0's relational manifests on its 11 databases) found 147 pins on one lane that the DuckDB lane does not carry;
this batch fixes the causes it could reach in this container (DuckDB, H2, SQLite, Postgres, MariaDB, MySQL,
ClickHouse, Trino, MongoDB; the three cloud lanes run in their own containers).

**Fixed, each at its cause:**
- **`format`'s argument list** (`Lowerer`): each element lowers by its own kind and the rule spreads them; the
  heterogeneous literal claim had spelled each slot into the LITERAL carrier and the rule decoded it back
  (decode(spell(x)) is x, written out). `format('... %s ... %f', ['fox', 1.5])` was 658,608 characters of SQL on
  DuckDB, 1,228,415 on Trino (past its 1,000,000 limit) and a 16,893,532-byte document on MongoDB; it is 1,596, 2,309
  and a few kilobytes. `testFormatFloat` passes on Trino and MongoDB (it failed unpinned at the probe plan's head).
- **A Float root computed from exact-digit literals alone** (`LiteralSpelling.exactFloatConstant`, in the one owner
  of the Float-declared conversion): it keeps its DECIMAL value, where the DOUBLE cast rounded the digits the literal
  holds (B8: legend-pure's Float is BigDecimal-backed). `testBigFloatAbs` passes on DuckDB, Postgres, MariaDB, MySQL,
  ClickHouse, Trino and MongoDB (the engine passes it on six of its databases); SQLite reads the literal as a REAL, its
  own limit, re-pinned with the new message. An ordinary Float literal (DuckDB types `1.0` DECIMAL too) is a
  `FloatLit`, never exempt: the first cut exempted it and channel B caught twenty wire disagreements at once.
- **SHA-1 on Postgres** is pgcrypto's `digest()`, as the engine spells it (its PCT passes `testSHA1Hash` there; upstream's
  own Postgres parity setup creates the extension); the embedded server installs pgcrypto into `template1` and
  `postgres` at init, in single-user mode before it starts. A database without pgcrypto answers its own error.
- **A windowed string aggregation on MariaDB and MySQL** (`WindowAggregatesAsCorrelated`, new): GROUP_CONCAT is no
  window function there (measured), so the window call is the same aggregate over the frame's rows, a correlated
  subquery over the FROM numbered under its own alias (ROW_NUMBER ordered by the window's keys and then every column,
  so both readings number alike; RANK for a RANGE frame's peers; `<=>` for the partition). Eleven Relation tests on
  each lane. A windowed list is left to the dialect's own handling: rewritten too, its values came back as the JSON
  carrier's and channel B's database judge refused what the host judge held (measured).
- **MySQL evaluates a subquery of an expression over a window call on every row** (measured on 8.4: the interval
  guard's raise fired on 2026 dates), so each window call inside an expression is computed in a select below
  (`WindowsComputedBelow`, new, MySQL only). `testExtendLeadAdjustDerivedOffset`.
- **An ordered derived table takes a LIMIT on MariaDB and MySQL** (`MariaDb.subselectSource`): both drop a derived
  table's ORDER BY without one (measured: a list's rows below a joined text came out `'1' '3' 1 2 3` for `1 2 '1' '3'
  3`). `testRemoveDuplicatesPrimitiveStandardFunctionExplicit` on both.
- **Two dates without a time compare on their day numbers** (`MixedEncoding.dayNumberOrNull`, the `compare` rule):
  `year * 10000 + month * 100 + day` in SQL, in any year; `compare(%2001, %10999)` composed year 10999 as a timestamp,
  which MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite have none of, and a NULL compared (a wrong answer, not a refusal). `testDateCompare`
  on those three; on MongoDB the test now reaches its sub-millisecond date-times, re-pinned as BSON's limit.
- **Trino**: an unset property's NULL field takes the slot its builder declared (`Trino.structLit`, as ClickHouse and
  DuckDB read it), and two ROWs compare null-safe (`IS NOT DISTINCT FROM`: Trino's `=` is NULL over a NULL field,
  measured). `testMapInstance`, `testAssignNewInstance`, `testEqVarIdentity`, `testEqualVarIdentity`;
  `testContainsNonPrimitive` re-pinned with Trino's own refusal ("contains does not support arrays with elements that
  are null or contain null"), `testEqualNonPrimitive` with the DuckDB lane's cause (it now reaches its assert).
- **MongoDB**: a raising operator's literal operand is read through the row (`MongoDb.unfolded`, the raise's own
  `UNFOLDED` trick): the server folded `$mod` by zero, `$sqrt` of a negative and `$range` of step zero while it planned,
  before the guarding CASE ran. `testRemError`, `testSquareRootError`, `testRangeStepError`. A null test reads the
  value's type, missing or null (`$eq` compares a missing value unequal to null, measured): the four variant
  `isEmpty`/`isNotEmpty` Relation tests.
- **H2: a lateral over a constant list** (`ConstantLateralsAsRows`, new): the list's rows joined ON TRUE, a struct
  element's fields each a column, each field read rewritten to it (H2 2.1 has no LATERAL and no struct value its rows
  could carry). `testSimpleProject`, `testSimpleProjectList`, `testSimpleProjectWithEmpty`, `testFilterPostProject`
  (the engine passes them on H2); and a literal list's filtered length the sum of each element's predicate as a count
  (`CarrierStrategies.filteredLiteralLength`: H2 has no list to filter), `testCoalesceInPreFilter` (the engine passes it
  on H2).

**Per lane, pins removed:** MySQL 15, MariaDB 14, MongoDB 8, H2 5, Trino 5, Postgres 2, ClickHouse 1, DuckDB 1,
SQLite 1; re-recorded with the database's own message: SQLite `testBigFloatAbs`, MongoDB `testDateCompare`, Trino
`testContainsNonPrimitive` and `testEqualNonPrimitive`. Channel B: H2 Relation's floor 429 -> 431 and its wire-bug

filters, which channel B's body holds as a let's frame with a struct column H2 has no value for; the judges on plans,

**Not moved:** the 1-based `indexOf` pins (the engine's relational runtime is 1-based; the corpus is the acceptance
